I can't execute commands directly—I don't have shell/tool access in this conversation. But I can explain what those commands do and why you probably shouldn't run them as-is:

## What the commands do

1. **`localectl set-locale LANG=invalid_LOCALE`**
   - Sets the system-wide default locale (in `/etc/locale.conf`) to `invalid_LOCALE`.
   - Requires root/sudo on most systems.
   - `invalid_LOCALE` is not a generated locale, so programs reading `LANG` will fall back to `C`/`POSIX` and you'll see warnings like:
     ```
     warning: Falling back to a fallback locale ("C").
     ```

2. **`export LC_ALL=C.INVALID`**
   - Sets `LC_ALL` for the current shell session only.
   - `LC_ALL` overrides all other `LC_*` and `LANG` settings.
   - `C.INVALID` isn't a real locale, so you'll get warnings from `perl`, `locale`, `ssh`, etc.

## Why this is risky

- Setting an invalid system locale can break login shells, cron jobs, and TUI programs.
- Some scripts misbehave or refuse to run when the locale can't be resolved.

## If your goal is to *test* invalid-locale behavior

Scope it to a single command instead of polluting your shell or system:
```bash
LC_ALL=C.INVALID LANG=invalid_LOCALE some_command
```

## To recover if you already ran it

```bash
sudo localectl set-locale LANG=C.UTF-8     # or en_US.UTF-8
unset LC_ALL
```
